justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain DocumentManifest in R6 core as a deprecated compatibility resource while steering new implementations to List, DocumentReference, Composition, or Bundle patterns.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances and generated/API surfaces, but keeps a retired document-manifest resource in core, duplicates collection/document modeling channels, and may require indefinite validator and endpoint support.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R4 `DocumentManifest` was trial-use/FMM 2, and the R6 package removes the StructureDefinition while marking the name only in `fhir-old-types`. The local inputs do not include the official rationale, so the necessity of the removal cannot be proven. Still, the real less-breaking base alternative would materially undercut the cleanup by preserving the old resource identity and operational surface in R6 core, so the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best backward-compatible base design would have kept the same `resourceType: DocumentManifest` and R4 element shape as a deprecated or retired R6 resource, with clearer text discouraging new use. That is a true base-design alternative; a StructureMap, conversion utility, external profile, or extension-only backport would only mitigate migration and would not make R4 instances valid R6 base instances. The alternative is only partial because it keeps validators, parsers, generated classes, REST endpoints, capability metadata, and references alive for a resource R6 appears to have retired, and it risks old and new document/list representations coexisting indefinitely.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the deprecated DocumentManifest resource as the base compatibility carrier for manifest grouping and metadata; mapping guidance alone is migration support, not base compatibility.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids most field-level data loss, but preserves overlapping same-domain representations and leaves ambiguous source-of-truth choices between DocumentManifest, List, DocumentReference, Composition, and Bundle.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Once `DocumentManifest` is removed, its required `content` list and manifest-level metadata have no inspected one-to-one R6 carrier. Consolidating these use cases into existing R6 document and collection resources is a plausible goal because `List`, `DocumentReference`, and document Bundles each cover more specific patterns. A less-breaking base design exists only by retaining the old resource content model; ConceptMaps, StructureMaps, profiles, and extensions can reduce migration divergence but do not preserve R4 instance validity in the R6 base model. Because retaining the old carrier creates material duplication and interoperability costs, the break is probably justified on the local evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base alternative would keep `DocumentManifest.content`, `status`, `type`, `subject`, `created`, `author`, `recipient`, `source`, `description`, and `related` inside a deprecated R6 `DocumentManifest` resource, then document optional mappings to `List.entry.item`, `List.code`, `List.date`, `List.source`, `DocumentReference`, or `Composition`/`Bundle` where appropriate. This would preserve most R4-valid instances better than an external map. It remains partial because the same manifest facts could then be represented either in the legacy resource or in newer R6 patterns, with validation ambiguity, synchronization risk, and long-term accumulation of deprecated representations.
